statement: Frontier 50%-success task time horizon >= 16 h (METR measurements, cross-checked against government AISI reports; by 2027-12-31)
status_at_phase_end: The 50%-success time-horizon metric was not yet published (first released Mar 2025). In-phase proxies: an independent evaluator found frontier agents matched what human baseliners do in ~30-35 minutes on its general autonomy suite (Aug-Oct 2024), and on 8-hour ML research-engineering tasks agents beat experts at a 2-hour budget but fell behind at 8 h and reached ~half of expert scores at 32 h (Nov 2024). Two government AI safety institutes began joint pre-deployment testing (Nov-Dec 2024). Frontier horizon at end-2024 thus well under 1 h on these proxies, far from 16 h.

items.summary: Independent evaluator: a frontier model agent with a basic scaffold completed ~40% of 77 general autonomy tasks, comparable to what human baseliners achieve in ~35 minutes; on 7 hard AI R&D tasks it matched professional ML engineers at a 2-hour limit but plateaued far below human 8-hour performance.
items.detail: METR, 'Details about METR's preliminary evaluation of Claude 3.5 Sonnet' (original 2024-06-20 model), 2024-10-30 (verified via search snippet). A similar ~35-minute level was reported for o1-preview (METR report, Sept 2024).

items.summary: Independent evaluator released an ML research-engineering benchmark (7 environments, 71 expert 8-hour attempts): best agents scored ~4x human experts at a 2-hour total budget, humans narrowly ahead at 8 hours, and ~2x the best agent at 32 hours. Agents iterate >10x faster and cheaper, but returns to longer time budgets are weak.
items.detail: METR, RE-Bench, 'Evaluating frontier AI R&D capabilities of language model agents against human experts', 2024-11-22 (verified via search snippet); models: Claude 3.5 Sonnet (new) and o1-preview.
items.value: humans 2x best agent at 32 h budget

items.summary: Two government AI safety institutes published their first joint pre-deployment test of a frontier model (biological, cyber, software and AI-development tasks, safeguard efficacy), establishing the government cross-check channel this indicator relies on; no time-horizon figure reported.
items.detail: Bloc A AISI and Bloc G AISI joint pre-deployment evaluation of Anthropic's upgraded Claude 3.5 Sonnet, report dated 2024-11-19 (verified via search snippet). A second joint report on OpenAI o1 followed in Dec 2024.

items.summary: No published 50%-success time-horizon series existed in 2024; the metric and its back-cast (including 2024 models) were first released in March 2025 and are excluded here under the as-of rule.
items.detail: METR, 'Measuring AI Ability to Complete Long Tasks', 2025-03-19 - outside phase window.
